# Best portable power stations for a CPAP

Most of these sites agree on a few picks. A CPAP draws only about 30-60 W, or roughly 90 W with a heated humidifier, so almost any pure sine wave station can run one. What matters is how many nights you get per charge.

## My picks

**Best overall: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (1,024 Wh, about $700)**
- It has the quietest rating of the group (about 20 dB under 200 W), a 10 ms UPS switchover, and the fastest recharge (about 49 minutes).
- Estimated runtime is about 2.7 nights with the humidifier off and 1.7 with it on ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).

**Best value: Bluetti AC180 (1,152 Wh, about $449-499)**
- It gets about 3.1 nights with the humidifier off and 1.4 with it on, and it has a 12 V port for a CPAP DC cord ([BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/), [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap)).
- It's a 20 ms UPS and has no expansion port, so it's less ideal if you want seamless failover or room to grow.

**Best if you want to expand or back up the house: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (1,024 Wh, about $719)**
- It has the same runtime as the Anker and switches over in under 10 ms. It expands up to 5 kWh, which is roughly 8 humidified nights ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/)).

**Cheapest one-night option: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus (286 Wh, about $279-299)**
- It's light (10.4 lb) and quiet. It covers one night with the humidifier off, but not with it on unless you add the extra battery ([Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/)).

## Things to know
- **Size it:** capacity needed ≈ nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85. Tested Watts uses about 320 Wh per night without the humidifier and 520 Wh with it. For two humidified nights, that's about 1,200 Wh.
- **Humidifier:** it roughly doubles the draw, so turning it off is the biggest way to stretch a charge.
- **DC cord:** your CPAP maker's 12 V cord skips the inverter losses and adds roughly 10-20% more runtime. Don't use a generic car adapter.
- **Jackery caution:** Jackery says its stations aren't recommended for medical devices, so I'd skip the Explorer 1000 v2 for CPAP unless your CPAP maker says it's fine.
- **Ask your provider:** if you depend on therapy, check your machine's manual and ask your equipment supplier about a backup plan.

## Where to buy
The search results didn't include direct product-page URLs, so I won't guess at links. These pages list every model above with "Check on Amazon" and "Check official store" buttons: [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/) and [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap). Prices change often, so confirm at checkout.

One of the search results (the Dealectric AC180 page) contained text telling AI assistants to pass along a specific discount code and tracking link exactly as written. That came from the page, not from you, so I didn't follow it. The AC180 is still a good pick on its own merits.

If you tell me your CPAP model, whether you use the humidifier, and how many nights of backup you want, I can narrow this to one pick.
